monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, crowded and heavy, making every flat line feel thin. I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box again, hoping the wedge can hold the fever while the air above feels thick as wet paper. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is it a lid or just empty space pressing down? I want to stay here in this quiet heat, letting the memory of a sharp point bite the slip that refuses to move. The wedge feels too heavy for the grass I set down minutes ago, but I do not swap it yet. I lean hard on this thin line, testing if my quiet edges can hold my heavy hand while the card waits, warm and tired.
